methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $129M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Candela is a Series C transportation company that has raised €129M+ to date. The broader transportation tech sector includes eight private comparables (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, ZeroAvia, and others) and no public peers, limiting direct valuation benchmarking.

Given the constrained peer set, stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method. Using total capital raised (€129M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement yields €219M. This reflects the capital efficiency and momentum expected at this stage, absent material operational deterioration or market dislocation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of €186M to €252M, with a median point of €219M. This range derives from sensitivity around the stage-progression multiplier (±15% variance). Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage or adjacent-stage peer transaction data in transportation, which limits confidence in the 1.7x multiplier's applicability to Candela specifically; cash burn trajectory and path to positive unit economics; and near-term funding environment conditions. A peer-median approach was not viable given insufficient same-stage or similar-tier comparables. Any valuation within this band should be stress-tested against Candela's specific burn rate, product-market traction, and cash runway.
